findings.summary: I read every required authority source in full, in Read calls of 120 lines or fewer: engineering README, ENGINEERING_DESIGN_V1.md v1.2 (lines 1–411), MODULE_GUIDE, REVIEW_NOTES, PRODUCT_V1 v0.4.1 (lines 1–262), the whole pinned PROJECT_CONTEXT v1.93 (lines 1–1292), AGENTS, SOURCE_OF_TRUTH, GOVERNANCE, APPROVALS (APPROVAL-007) and SYNTHETIC_CONSENT_ONBOARDING_TRACK. I then checked the actual source at 8321317 against the card and the 2026-11-12 revision. On the server side, every operation runs inside accepted withSession, and the latest consent row is locked FOR UPDATE before any private rows. The context fence and owned-child membership checks come before the receipt lookup. The exact receipt and the equivalent initial create return before CAS or quota. Siblings are explicit, corrections append history under CAS, migration 008 has deferred triggers and cascades, and the HTTP union and setup allowlist are scoped exactly. This matches engineering v1.2 ADR-E02 and the WM-02 consent-before-child-write rule, with PD-003 sibling isolation and PD-014 withdrawal fencing. All three card acceptance criteria are met and backed by real evidence: 67/67 app tests, the build, the full card checker including the protected child probe (quota/429, conflicts, cross-household, retained-data fence, household cascade), and a native CUA record whose source blobs match 832's LoopChildSetup.tsx (730c189), child-setup.mjs (0d9f879) and loop-child-setup.css (39a280e). Every review1 correction is present in the source. A failed passive refresh now clears private intent only on a confirmed 403 and keeps the sticky save error. A real HTTP/React test proves that a lost sibling acknowledgment, then a failed passive GET, then Retry resends the same UUID and adds no extra child or receipt. App-level static-shell route tests and 44px links are in place, the unavailable/unexpected 503 alias is documented, and the native held-GET observation was run on 832. Real consent wording, the G-E03/10-A privacy review, retained-data handling, providers and public access all stay closed and are not claimed as resolved.
